title: QMX: how the agent system fits together
audience: Mubarak. Plain words. The lead renders this as an animated one-page explainer.

system_steps.title: You talk to one copilot
system_steps.caption: There is one copilot. You talk to it wherever you are. It never does long work itself; it hands work out and explains results.

system_steps.title: Your settings and the safety rules sit above everything
system_steps.caption: Model choices, spending limits and the checks live in Settings. The harness keeps money read-only and asks you when it must.

system_steps.title: The engine runs recipes while you sleep
system_steps.caption: A recipe is a list of steps. Cheap steps are scripts. The engine saves every finished step, pauses at your usage cap, and never redoes paid work.

system_steps.title: Everything is a folder
system_steps.caption: Agents, workflows, skills, packs, mini apps and methodologies are folders of one shape. Old versions are kept; nothing is deleted.

system_steps.title: A session is born in a home and carries its packs
system_steps.caption: A session born in the Lab keeps its Lab tools even when you open it in the copilot. Packs add reach; the stricter rule wins.

system_steps.title: Work lands in rooms
system_steps.caption: The Lab and Board, the Library called Strats, Portfolio, mini apps and the QMX browser. Agents read money and never move it.

system_steps.title: The trading node stays outside
system_steps.caption: A unit is a strategy with its risk settings. It lives in the node, a server you upload it to. Agents only read facts from it.

system_steps.title: Every result is checked, then drawn
system_steps.caption: Agents produce data, not pages. A checker confirms every number has a source. Then QMX draws one of six fixed page types.

decisions.question: Inside the Lab, may agents start and schedule their own jobs without asking you, as long as background use stays under your 50% cap? (This changes your 10-13 rule that scheduling always asks.)
decisions.why: Without it every unattended Lab run stops at its first ask.

decisions.question: When something proven in the Lab goes into Strats, should QMX just tell you instead of asking first?
decisions.why: Otherwise every promotion parks a run until you answer.

decisions.question: Agents must ask you before one run spends more than $___ on paid keys such as OpenRouter. What number? (Or say "always ask".)
decisions.recommended: Always ask, until you pick a number
decisions.why: Only you can set a money number. No run spends keys without it.

decisions.question: Lift the browser hold for one first step: a separate QMX browser you log into once and can watch live, which agents use to read pages, one job at a time, with no clicking?
decisions.why: The funnel needs TradingView and playlist pages. Read-only keeps the hold's spirit.

decisions.question: Rules like "a run may not skip a check" bind agents only. You can drop any check in your own workflows, and the result shows a badge. Agree?
decisions.why: Total creative freedom for you; the brakes stay on the agents.

decisions.question: May the Experimentation Board be saved on the backend, so a board survives restarts and workflows can run it? (This changes two docs that say the Board lives only in the browser.)
decisions.why: A board that vanishes on restart cannot be run overnight.

decisions.question: Build order: a small paper scout runs first, only as a quiet test that the engine works. Then the Lab and Board (the first thing built for you), then one mini app as a plugin. The morning brief and Portfolio reports come later. Agree?
decisions.why: The Lab is the core. Desk briefs need a trading node that is not ready.

decisions.question: Urgent alerts: which phone channel may QMX send to, if any? (Until you pick one, everything goes to the in-app inbox.)
decisions.recommended: Inbox only, until you pick a channel
decisions.why: Sending to your phone is sending on your behalf; the channel is yours.
